scenes.title: The Big Blue Home
narration: Look outside, have you ever wondered what makes our home planet so special?
Earth is like a giant ball spinning in the deep dark space.
It is the only place we know that has life, air, and water.

scenes.title: Land and Water
narration: If you look at a globe, you will see mostly blue colors.
That blue is our vast oceans, like the Indian Ocean near our shores.
The green and brown parts are the land where we live and play.
These large pieces of land are called continents.

scenes.title: Living on Earth
narration: Think of a tall mountain like the Himalayas in the north of India.
Or think of the holy Ganga river flowing down to the plains.
All these landforms make Earth a beautiful place for animals and humans.

scenes.title: Caring for Earth
narration: Earth gives us everything we need, so we must be kind to it.
We can help by planting trees, saving water, and keeping our parks clean.
What is one thing you can do today to keep our Earth happy?

scenes.title: Where are we going
narration: Have you ever looked at a map and wondered what those tiny pictures mean?
Maps help us find our way around places like Delhi or Mumbai.
But maps are small, so they use special symbols to show big things.

scenes.title: Understanding map symbols
narration: A map symbol is a tiny drawing that stands for a real object.
Instead of drawing a whole forest, maps show a small tree symbol.
A blue line often tells you there is a river nearby.
Every map has a key, which acts like a secret code dictionary.

scenes.title: Reading a park map
narration: Let us look at a map of a park in your neighborhood.
We see a small red triangle symbol for the park entrance.
A yellow square symbol shows exactly where the swing set is.
Now we can walk straight to the swings without getting lost.

scenes.title: Recap and explore
narration: Symbols make maps easy to read by replacing big objects with drawings.
Always check the map key to understand what the symbols mean.
Think about it: If you were making a map, what symbol would you draw for your school?

scenes.title: The Big Blue Planet
narration: Have you ever looked at a globe and wondered why it is so blue?
Our Earth is covered mostly by water, but we have big lands too.
Today, let's explore where the land ends and the water begins.

scenes.title: Continents and Oceans
narration: Large pieces of land on Earth are called continents.
The huge, salty bodies of water surrounding them are called oceans.
There are seven continents and five big oceans in total.
We live in Asia, the largest continent of them all.

scenes.title: Land and Water Together
narration: Think of the mighty Ganga river flowing across the land.
The river starts in the mountains and rushes down to the sea.
It gives water to farms, helping crops grow for our food.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: Earth has land for us to live on and water for us to drink.
Both land and water are precious, so we must keep them clean.
Think about it: What is your favorite place to visit, a mountain or the beach?

scenes.title: Where are we going
narration: Have you ever been lost in a big park or a busy market?
It is easy to get turned around when everything looks new.
How do we know which way to walk to find our friends?

scenes.title: The Four Main Directions
narration: Maps use four main directions to help us find our way.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
North is always at the top, and South is at the bottom.
We call this a compass rose on a map.

scenes.title: Walking to the Sweet Shop
narration: Let's help Rohan walk from his home to the sweet shop.
First, he walks North past the big banyan tree.
Then, he turns East to reach the shop for delicious jalebis.
By following these steps, he arrives safely every time.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Directions
narration: Remember, maps always use North, South, East, and West.
Using these helps us explore our beautiful India confidently.
Think about it: If you face the rising sun, which direction is behind you?

scenes.title: A World in Your Hands
narration: Have you ever wondered why our Earth looks like a big blue ball?
Meet Rohan, he has a small model of the Earth on his desk.
This model is called a globe and it shows us our whole world.

scenes.title: How the Globe Works
narration: The globe is a perfect map shaped exactly like our planet.
See the blue parts? That is all the water in our oceans.
The colorful parts are the different countries where people live.
Globes show us that the Earth is round, not flat like a paper map.

scenes.title: Finding India on the Globe
narration: Let us spin the globe to find our beautiful country, India.
It is in the southern part of the continent called Asia.
Notice how India is surrounded by water on three sides.
Even the giant Himalayan mountains are marked on this tiny globe.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Globes show us the Earth's true round shape and where lands are.
We use blue for water and colors for different countries.
Think about it: If you could travel anywhere, where would you point on the globe?

scenes.title: Where do we live?
narration: Look at this blue marble floating in space.
Have you ever wondered what makes up our huge home?
It is made of giant land pieces and deep blue water.

scenes.title: Continents and Oceans
narration: The seven giant land areas are called continents.
Our own India is in the big continent called Asia.
The five huge salty water bodies are called oceans.
The Indian Ocean is named right after our country.

scenes.title: Exploring the Map
narration: Imagine an explorer traveling from Asia to Africa.
They cross the blue Indian Ocean on a big ship.
The map shows land as green and water as blue.

scenes.title: Wrapping it up
narration: Earth has seven continents and five vast oceans.
Everything is connected to make our home special.
Think about it: which continent would you like to visit one day?

scenes.title: Getting Lost in the Park
narration: Have you ever wondered how to find your way in a big place like Cubbon Park?
Imagine you are lost and need to find the exit gate quickly.
A map is like a secret treasure guide that shows us exactly where things are.

scenes.title: Secrets of the Map
narration: Every good map has a title to tell us what place we are looking at.
The legend or key explains what the little symbols on the map really mean.
Directions like North, South, East, and West help us know which way to walk.

scenes.title: Using a Map in India
narration: Let us look at a map of a school playground in Delhi.
The blue line shows the path to the water fountain.
The small green triangle shows where the big mango tree stands.
We follow these symbols to walk safely to our destination.

scenes.title: Remembering Your Map Skills
narration: Maps use symbols and legends to help us explore our world.
Always check the compass rose to know your direction before you start.
If you had to draw a map of your bedroom, what symbols would you use?

scenes.title: The Big Mountain Question
narration: Have you ever seen a giant hill touching the clouds while visiting a place like Shimla?
Those are mountains, the tallest landforms on our beautiful Earth.
Why do these huge mountains stand so tall above everything else?

scenes.title: How Mountains Are Made
narration: Under the ground, giant pieces of rock slowly push against each other.
This slow squeeze makes the land fold and rise upwards over millions of years.
That is how a bumpy, snowy mountain peak is born.
Mountains are much higher and steeper than the small hills near your school.

scenes.title: The Great Himalayas
narration: In India, we have the mighty Himalayas stretching across the north.
Mount Everest is the tallest peak in the whole world, found right there.
Many big rivers like the Ganga start their journey as melting ice here.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Mountains are tall landforms created by the Earth pushing rocks together.
They give us beautiful views, cool weather, and start our mighty rivers.
If you could climb to the very top, what would you see first?

scenes.title: The Big World Shrinker
narration: Have you ever wondered how a whole country fits on one small piece of paper?
We use a secret tool called a scale to make everything smaller.
Let us see how we can map your home town.

scenes.title: Learning the Secret Code
narration: A scale tells us that a tiny distance on paper equals a huge distance.
If 1 centimeter on the map equals 10 kilometers in real life, we can measure far.
This helps us know how long a trip to the market will take.

scenes.title: A Trip to Delhi
narration: Imagine we are measuring the distance from your school to India Gate.
We place our ruler on the map and find it is 5 centimeters long.
Since 1 centimeter is 10 kilometers, we multiply 5 times 10.
That means India Gate is 50 kilometers away from our school.

scenes.title: Mapping Made Easy
narration: Maps use scales to shrink the world so we can hold it in our hands.
Always check the corner of the map to find your special scale code.
Think about it: if you drew your bedroom on paper, what scale would you use?

scenes.title: The Big Hill Mystery
narration: Have you ever climbed a small hill near your home or school?
A hill is a piece of land that is higher than the ground around it.
But why are some places so much higher than others?

scenes.title: Understanding How Hills Work
narration: Hills are smaller and rounder than giant mountains.
They are formed when the earth's surface pushes up over a long time.
Many hills are covered with thick, green trees and pretty flowers.
They often have cool air because they are high up in the sky.

scenes.title: Hills in Incredible India
narration: In India, the Nilgiri Hills in the south are famous for tea gardens.
Farmers work hard to plant tea bushes on the sloping land.
Many people visit hill stations like Ooty to see the mist.
The soil there is perfect for growing tasty tea leaves.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Hills are raised land, smaller than mountains, and often very cool.
They provide homes for special plants and beautiful tea gardens.
If you could build a house on a hill, what would you see from your window?

scenes.title: The High Tableland
narration: Have you ever climbed a hill and found a flat area on top?
It looks just like a giant table in the middle of the landscape.
This special landform is called a plateau.

scenes.title: How Plateaus Form
narration: Plateaus are high above the land around them.
They have steep sides that go down to the plains.
The top part is usually very flat or gently rolling.
Nature builds these over millions of years with forces from deep underground.

scenes.title: India's Deccan Plateau
narration: In India, we have the famous Deccan Plateau in the south.
It is covered in rich soil that is great for growing cotton.
Many rivers flow through this area, giving water to farms.
It is home to many cities, forests, and animals like elephants.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: A plateau is a high landform with a flat top and steep sides.
India's Deccan Plateau is a perfect example of this amazing landform.
Think about it: Why do you think people build cities on flat plateaus?

scenes.title: The Flat Green Land
narration: Have you ever looked at a field that stretches as far as you can see?
This big, flat land is what we call a plain.
Why is this flat ground so special for our country?

scenes.title: How Plains Are Made
narration: Rivers flow down from the tall mountains carrying bits of soil.
This rich soil spreads out over the land when rivers flood.
Over many years, this creates deep, flat, and super healthy ground.

scenes.title: Life in the Gangetic Plains
narration: In India, the Northern Plains are fed by the mighty Ganga river.
Farmers here grow delicious wheat, rice, and golden sugarcane.
Because the land is flat, it is easy to build roads and houses.
This is why so many people choose to live here.

scenes.title: A Quick Wrap Up
narration: Plains are flat lands created by rivers bringing rich soil.
They are perfect for farming and building big cities.
Think about it: If you could build a new town, would you pick a flat plain or a mountain?

scenes.title: A Trip to the Mountains
narration: Have you ever looked at big mountains and wondered about the low space between them?
That low, flat area between hills or mountains is called a valley.
Let's find out how these beautiful valleys are made in our incredible India.

scenes.title: How Valleys Are Formed
narration: Many valleys are carved by powerful rivers flowing down from high peaks.
Over millions of years, the rushing water cuts deep into the ground.
This process makes a wide, V-shaped path between the tall slopes.
Sometimes, huge moving ice called glaciers also scrape the earth to form U-shaped valleys.

scenes.title: The Beautiful Kullu Valley
narration: Look at the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh, fed by the Beas River.
The river brings fresh water, making the valley floor rich and green.
Farmers grow delicious apples here because the soil is perfect for them.
People love visiting these valleys for the cool air and amazing views.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: So, valleys are low lands formed by rivers or ice between mountains.
They provide fertile soil for farming and beautiful homes for many people.
Think about it: if you lived in a valley, would you climb the mountain or stay below?

scenes.title: Where does water start?
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in a river comes from?
It all begins high up in the cold mountains.
Snow melts into tiny streams that trickle down the rocks.

scenes.title: How rivers grow bigger
narration: As the streams move down, they join together to form a river.
Small rivers meet bigger ones called tributaries.
The water flows faster as it travels through the land.

scenes.title: A river in India
narration: The Ganga is a famous river that starts in the Himalayas.
It flows through many cities like Haridwar and Varanasi.
Finally, the river reaches the sea and mixes with the ocean.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Rivers start in mountains, grow by joining streams, and end in the sea.
Rivers provide water for our farms, our homes, and for nature.
Think about it: What would happen to our town if the river stopped flowing?

scenes.title: Looking at the Lake
narration: Have you ever visited a calm lake like Dal Lake in Kashmir?
Unlike a river that flows fast, a lake stays in one place.
Do you wonder how all that water stays inside the bowl?

scenes.title: How Lakes Form
narration: A lake is a large pool of water surrounded by land.
Rainwater or melting snow fills up a deep hole in the ground.
Sometimes, rivers flow into the lake, keeping it nice and full.

scenes.title: Example: Loktak Lake
narration: Look at Loktak Lake in Manipur, famous for its floating islands.
The water here helps local farmers grow rice and catch fish.
The lake acts like a giant, natural water tank for everyone.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Lakes
narration: Lakes are still bodies of water held by the earth.
They collect rain and provide homes for many plants and animals.
Can you think of a lake near your town or village?

scenes.title: A Land of Sand
narration: Have you ever seen a place with endless sand and very little water?
This is the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, a place full of surprises.
Why is it so hot and dry here? Let us find out!

scenes.title: What Makes a Desert
narration: Deserts are places that get very little rain throughout the year.
The sun shines brightly, making the sand feel very warm.
Plants here have special ways to save every drop of water.

scenes.title: Life in the Thar
narration: Camels are the ships of the desert, walking easily on sand.
People wear bright turbans and colorful clothes to stay cool.
Thorny bushes and shrubs grow where water is hard to find.
They might travel long distances to find a village well.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Desert
narration: The Thar Desert is dry, hot, and full of amazing life.
Animals and plants adapt to live with very little water.
Think about it: How would you stay cool if you lived in the desert?

scenes.title: The Community Around Us
narration: Look around your neighborhood in Delhi or Mumbai, what do you see?
People live and work together in groups called communities.
Have you ever wondered why we all do things differently?

scenes.title: What Makes A Community
narration: A community is a group of people who share a common life.
We might speak different languages or celebrate different festivals.
Even with differences, we help each other every single day.
Our common rules help us live in harmony and peace.

scenes.title: A Real Indian Example
narration: Imagine a busy street market in Kolkata, filled with many families.
Shopkeepers sell sweets like Rasgulla to people from all backgrounds.
Neighbors share smiles and help carry heavy bags for elders.
This kindness shows how we are one big community.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Communities are groups of people living and helping each other.
We respect our differences to make our country stronger.
Think about it, how can you help your community today?

Rivers and Water Bodies: Importance of W.topic: Rivers and Water Bodies: Importance of Water
Rivers and Water Bodies: Importance of W.title: Our Magic Blue Planet

scenes.title: Where does water come from?
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in your school bottle comes from?
We use water for drinking, washing, and keeping our bodies cool.
Today, let's follow the journey of water across our beautiful India.

scenes.title: How rivers start their journey
narration: Most rivers start high up in the cold, snowy Himalayan mountains.
As the snow melts, it forms tiny streams that flow downhill.
These streams join together to become a wide, powerful, rushing river.
The river carries fresh water all the way to our farms.

scenes.title: The Ganga River Story
narration: Look at the Ganga, one of India's most important rivers.
It starts at Gangotri and travels across many states.
People use the water to grow wheat, rice, and vegetables.
Finally, the Ganga meets the sea at the Bay of Bengal.

scenes.title: Keeping our water clean
narration: Rivers give us life, so we must keep them clean.
Never throw plastic or trash into our rivers or lakes.
Think about it: how can you save water at home today?

Rivers and Water Bodies: Seas.title: Journey to the Big Blue Sea

scenes.title: The Big Blue Question
narration: Have you ever visited a beach in Mumbai or Puri and seen the water go on forever?
That giant body of salty water is called a sea.
Where does all that water actually come from?

scenes.title: Rivers Meet the Sea
narration: Rivers start high up in the mountains as fresh, clean water.
They flow through towns and fields, picking up tiny bits of salt from rocks.
Finally, the river reaches the end and pours into the sea.
The water stays in the sea, and the salt builds up over a long time.

scenes.title: India's Beautiful Coastline
narration: India has the Arabian Sea on the west and the Bay of Bengal on the east.
These seas are home to colorful fish, turtles, and many underwater plants.
Fishermen use boats to catch food for us to eat at home.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Seas
narration: Rivers carry water to the sea, making it salty over millions of years.
Our seas are precious homes for animals and help us in many ways.
Think about it: Why do you think we must keep our beaches clean?

scenes.title: Where does the river go?
narration: Have you ever seen the river flowing near your school or home?
It moves along the land, but where does all that water end up?
All rivers eventually meet the deep, vast ocean.

scenes.title: What is an ocean?
narration: The ocean is a massive body of salty water covering most of Earth.
Unlike rivers, ocean water is too salty for us to drink.
It is home to amazing creatures like whales, dolphins, and colorful fish.

scenes.title: India's beautiful coastlines
narration: India is surrounded by water on three sides, like a peninsula.
To the west, we have the Arabian Sea near Mumbai.
To the east, the Bay of Bengal touches the shores of Chennai.
And down south, the vast Indian Ocean waits for us.

scenes.title: Remembering our blue planet
narration: Rivers flow into oceans, and oceans hold most of Earths water.
We must keep our rivers and beaches clean to protect sea life.
Think about it, what would happen if all the ice turned into ocean water?

scenes.title: How We Say Hello
narration: Have you noticed that your friends speak different languages at home?
Some say Namaste, some say Sat Sri Akal, and others say Vanakkam.
Why do people in India use so many different languages to talk?

scenes.title: Our Language Roots
narration: India is like a giant garden with many different flowers.
Each language has its own special sounds and beautiful writing style.
Families pass these languages down to their children over many years.
It is how we tell stories and share our unique culture.

scenes.title: A Day In India
narration: Imagine Rohan in Delhi who speaks Hindi with his grandmother.
He travels to Kerala and hears people speaking Malayalam at the market.
They both use English at school so everyone can understand each other.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Words
narration: Our country has twenty-two official languages in our Constitution.
Learning a new language is like opening a secret treasure chest.
Which new language would you love to learn to speak today?

People and Communities: Food.title: Where Does Our Food Come From?

scenes.title: The Yummy Breakfast Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered where the yummy paratha on your plate actually comes from?
It starts with ingredients like wheat flour, oil, and spices from our pantry.
But how did these things get to our kitchen in the first place?

scenes.title: From Farms to Our Kitchens
narration: Farmers work hard in the fields to grow wheat and vegetables under the sun.
After the harvest, trucks carry the crops to the local mandi, or market.
Shopkeepers buy these goods so parents like yours can shop for dinner.

scenes.title: The Journey of Milk
narration: Let us look at milk, which comes from healthy cows and buffaloes on farms.
The milk is cleaned and packed into pouches at a big dairy factory.
Finally, the delivery person brings the milk to our doorstep every morning.

scenes.title: Recapping Our Food Journey
narration: Food travels from farms to markets, and finally reaches our home kitchens.
Many people work together to make sure we have healthy meals every day.
Think about it: which food item on your plate traveled the longest distance today?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you noticed how your home looks different from a house in the snowy mountains?
Some houses are made of bricks, while others are made of bamboo or wood.
Why do people build their houses in such different ways across India?

scenes.title: Climate and Shelter
narration: Houses are built to protect us from the weather outside.
In hot places like Rajasthan, thick walls keep the inside cool.
In rainy places like Assam, houses stand on tall wooden poles.
This stops floodwater from entering the living area.

scenes.title: Materials Nearby
narration: Builders use materials they find easily in their own neighborhood.
In mountain villages, builders use local stone and wood for warmth.
In big cities like Mumbai, we use concrete and steel to build tall apartments.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Houses change based on the weather and the materials available nearby.
Every house, big or small, keeps our families safe and happy.
Think about it: what materials are used to build the houses in your street?

scenes.title: Clothes Around Us
narration: Have you noticed how your friends wear different clothes to school or a wedding?
Why do people in India wear such different outfits depending on where they live?
Let's explore why our clothes are so special and different!

scenes.title: Weather and Comfort
narration: First, the weather tells us what to wear to stay comfortable.
In the hot summers of Rajasthan, people wear light cotton to stay cool.
In the snowy mountains of Ladakh, thick wool keeps everyone warm.
We choose fabrics that help our bodies feel just right.

scenes.title: Tradition and Culture
narration: Next, our clothes show our family traditions and festivals.
Rohan wears a bright Kurta for Diwali, while Zara wears a beautiful Salwar Kameez.
Many states have their own special weaving styles, like the Kanjeevaram silk from Tamil Nadu.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: So, we dress for the weather and to celebrate our unique culture.
Our clothing tells a story about where we live and who we are.
Think about it: If you moved to a new state, would you change your clothes?

scenes.title: The Joy Of Celebrations
narration: Have you ever wondered why we celebrate Diwali or Eid with special meals and clothes?
Traditions are the fun things we do together that connect us to our family history.
Let us explore why these habits make our communities feel so strong and happy.

scenes.title: What Are Traditions?
narration: A tradition is a custom passed down from our grandparents to our parents and then to us.
It can be a special dish like delicious Biryani made every Sunday at home.
It can also be a unique dance or a festival song we sing during celebrations.
These traditions help us remember where we come from and who we are.

scenes.title: A Day Of Pongal
narration: Think of the harvest festival Pongal celebrated in Tamil Nadu every January.
Families wake up early to boil fresh rice in a decorated clay pot.
They share this sweet dish with neighbors to say thank you for the harvest.
By doing this together, everyone in the village feels like one big family.

scenes.title: Keep The Traditions Alive
narration: Traditions keep our culture alive and teach us how to care for one another.
They remind us of our past while bringing us closer in the present.
Think about it: what is one special tradition your family follows every single year?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered how your school bag is made?
Everything we use starts as raw materials from nature.
Industry is how we turn those materials into things we need.

scenes.title: How Industry Works
narration: First, workers collect raw materials like cotton or wood.
Then, big machines in factories process these materials.
Finally, the finished products are packed and shipped to shops.
This process is called manufacturing.

scenes.title: Making Cotton Shirts
narration: Let us see how a cotton shirt is made in India.
Farmers grow soft cotton plants in the warm fields.
A factory spins the cotton into long, strong threads.
Machines weave the thread into cloth and sew the shirt.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Industry turns raw materials into useful products using machines.
It helps us get clothes, food, and toys for our homes.
Think about it: what is one object in your room that was made in a factory?

scenes.title: Where does our food come
narration: Have you ever wondered where your tasty lunch comes from?
It all starts with a very special job called farming.
Farmers work hard every day to grow the food we eat.

scenes.title: Steps to grow our food
narration: First, the farmer prepares the soil by digging and cleaning it.
Next, they plant seeds carefully in neat, straight rows.
Then, they provide plenty of water and pull out unwanted weeds.
Finally, when the plants are ready, the farmer harvests the crop.

scenes.title: Example of wheat farming
narration: In Punjab, farmers grow golden wheat under the bright sun.
The stalks grow tall and change from green to golden yellow.
The harvested wheat is sent to mills to become flour.
Finally, your mother buys it to make delicious hot rotis.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: Farming involves planting, caring for, and harvesting crops for food.
Without our farmers, we would not have healthy food to eat.
Think about it: What is your favorite vegetable, and how do you think it grows?

scenes.title: The Busy Neighborhood
narration: Look around your street in Delhi, who do you see working?
From the milkman to the doctor, everyone provides a service.
Have you ever wondered why we need these different jobs?

scenes.title: Understanding Community Services
narration: A service is work someone does to help others.
Some services keep us safe, like our brave police officers.
Others keep us healthy, like the nurse at the clinic.
We pay for these services using money like rupees.

scenes.title: A Day With Rohan
narration: Rohan wakes up and picks up his newspaper from the delivery person.
At school, his teacher explains a fun math lesson.
After school, he visits the local cobbler to fix his shoe.
Rohan realizes his day was easy because of these helpers.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Services are jobs that make our daily lives run smoothly.
Every helper, from the postman to the farmer, is important.
Think about it: Which community helper would you miss the most?

scenes.title: The Village Problem
narration: Have you ever wondered who fixes the broken streetlights in your village?
Meet Rohan, he lives in a busy village in Rajasthan.
He sees a messy park and wants to know who helps clean it up.

scenes.title: Meet the Gram Panchayat
narration: In India, our villages are looked after by a group called the Gram Panchayat.
The head of this group is called the Sarpanch.
They are chosen by the villagers to make important decisions for everyone.

scenes.title: Working for the Village
narration: Rohan goes to the Panchayat meeting with his father.
They discuss using village money to buy new swings and clean water pipes.
The Sarpanch listens to everyone and signs the plan to start the work.

scenes.title: Why It Matters
narration: The Gram Panchayat keeps our village clean, safe, and happy for all.
They build schools, roads, and look after our health clinics too.
Think about it: If you were the Sarpanch, what would you fix first in your village?

scenes.title: A Problem in the Village
narration: Have you seen a broken street light or a dirty pond in your village?
Who helps fix these things when the village needs help?
Meet the Panchayat, our local village government team!

scenes.title: What is the Panchayat
narration: The Panchayat is a group of leaders chosen by the village people.
They meet to talk about how to make the village better.
The head of this group is called the Sarpanch.

scenes.title: Helping the Village Grow
narration: Imagine the village needs a new paved road to school.
The Panchayat decides to use village funds to buy materials.
Workers build the road so children can walk safely.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The Panchayat listens to us and solves local problems.
They help keep our water, roads, and schools in good shape.
If you were Sarpanch, what one thing would you fix in your village?

scenes.title: Why So Many Festivals
narration: Have you noticed how often we celebrate with sweets and new clothes?
India is like a big family with many different traditions.
Why do we have so many festivals all year round?

scenes.title: Celebrating Through The Year
narration: Festivals mark the changing seasons and our history.
We celebrate harvest, legends, and the victory of good over evil.
Every community brings their own unique colors to India.

scenes.title: A Look At Diwali
narration: Let us look at Diwali, the beautiful festival of lights.
Families clean their homes and draw colorful rangoli on the floor.
We light clay lamps and share delicious mithai with friends.

scenes.title: The Spirit Of Unity
narration: Festivals remind us that we are all part of one nation.
They teach us to love our neighbors and respect different ways.
Think about it: which festival makes your family happiest and why?

scenes.title: The Messy Park Problem
narration: Look at our park, it is full of trash today.
Who should we call to help clean this up?
Let us learn about our local municipality.

scenes.title: What is a Municipality
narration: A municipality is a group of people elected to look after our town.
They work in an office called the Municipal Corporation.
Their job is to keep our streets safe and clean.
They use money from taxes to build parks and roads.

scenes.title: Helping Our Neighborhood
narration: When the street lights go out, the municipality fixes them.
They send trucks to collect our daily garbage.
They also keep our local water supply clean and safe.
They even look after local schools and hospitals.

scenes.title: Wrap Up and Think
narration: The municipality keeps our town running smoothly every day.
We help them by keeping our own homes tidy.
Think about it: what is one thing you would improve in your town?

scenes.title: The World of Work
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes your colorful clothes or the clay pots at home?
Many people in India practice special jobs that have been passed down for generations.
These are called traditional occupations, and they are a big part of our culture.

scenes.title: Learning the Craft
narration: A traditional occupation uses skills learned from family members instead of just schools.
Craftspeople use natural materials like cotton, clay, wood, or metal to create things.
They work with their hands to make unique items that machines cannot easily copy.

scenes.title: Meet the Weaver
narration: Let us visit a weaver in Varanasi who creates beautiful silk sarees on a loom.
First, the weaver dyes the silk threads in bright, cheerful colors.
Then, they carefully weave the threads on a wooden loom to make a pattern.
Finally, they sell their finished work at the local market for rupees.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Workers
narration: Traditional jobs keep our history alive and help our local communities grow.
We should respect these talented people who share their hard work with us.
Think about it: What is one traditional craft you have seen in your own city?

scenes.title: Why do we dance?
narration: Have you ever seen dancers spinning at a wedding or a school festival?
In India, dance is not just moving, it is a way to tell stories.
Do you wonder how dancers tell these stories without saying a single word?

scenes.title: The Language of Hands
narration: Indian classical dancers use their hands to make special shapes called mudras.
A lotus flower can be shown by opening your palms slowly.
Each mudra acts like a word in a secret dance language.

scenes.title: A Story in Motion
narration: Look at a Kathak dancer from North India wearing many silver bells.
When they tap their feet, the bells make a rhythmic sound like raindrops.
They spin fast to show the wind blowing through the trees.
They use their eyes and faces to show if they feel happy or sad.

scenes.title: Dancing Through History
narration: India has many beautiful dances, like Bharatanatyam from the sunny south.
These dances keep our traditions and history alive for everyone to see.
Think about it: if you had to tell a story with your hands, what would you say?

scenes.title: The Messy Park Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered who cleans up the park after a fun festival?
Arjun was playing cricket and saw the bins were full and needed clearing.
It is not magic, but our local government working hard for us!

scenes.title: What is Local Government
narration: The local government is a team elected to manage our neighborhood needs.
In big cities, this is called the Municipal Corporation.
In smaller towns, we call it the Municipal Council.

scenes.title: Keeping Our Streets Clean
narration: The workers collect garbage from our homes every single morning.
They make sure the street lights turn on when the sun goes down.
They also keep the public water taps working for everyone to use.

scenes.title: Our Role as Citizens
narration: We help the government by putting litter only in the dustbins.
Together, we keep our community clean, safe, and happy for everyone.
Think about it: What is one thing you can do to help your neighborhood?

scenes.title: Music Is Everywhere
narration: Have you heard the rhythmic beat of a dholak during a festival?
Music is a special part of how we celebrate in India.
Do you know how these beautiful sounds are made?

scenes.title: Two Main Styles
narration: In North India, we often hear Hindustani classical music.
Down South, we enjoy the beautiful Carnatic music tradition.
Both styles use ragas, which are special melodic patterns.
They also follow talas, which keep the rhythmic beat.

scenes.title: Famous Musical Instruments
narration: The sitar is a string instrument that creates sweet melodies.
The tabla has two drums that keep a steady beat.
And the flute, or bansuri, sounds like a gentle breeze.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: India has diverse music styles like Hindustani and Carnatic.
Instruments like the sitar and tabla bring songs to life.
Think about it: which musical instrument would you like to learn to play?

scenes.title: The Sounds Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered why your friends speak different languages at home?
India is a huge country with people from many different backgrounds.
Today, let us explore the beautiful languages spoken across our land.

scenes.title: Many Ways To Speak
narration: In India, we have hundreds of languages and thousands of dialects.
Hindi is spoken by many people, especially in North India.
In the South, you will hear beautiful languages like Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada.
Bengali, Marathi, and Gujarati are also spoken by millions of happy citizens.

scenes.title: A Day With Friends
narration: Imagine Rohan in Delhi says Namaste to greet his teacher.
In Chennai, Meera says Vanakkam to her friends at school.
Even though they use different words, they both mean hello with kindness.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Differences
narration: Languages make India a colorful and special place to live.
Respecting every language helps us all stay united as one nation.
Think about it: How many different languages can you say hello in?

scenes.title: The Magic of Flavors
narration: Have you ever wondered why your lunch smells so delicious and different every day?
India is a huge country with many different regions and traditions.
Each place uses local ingredients to make special meals for their families.

scenes.title: Spices and Grains
narration: In the north, we love soft rotis made from golden wheat flour.
In the south, people enjoy fluffy idlis and crunchy dosas made from rice.
Spices like turmeric and cumin give our food its bright color and zing.

scenes.title: Making a Yummy Dosa
narration: First, we soak rice and lentils to make a smooth, bubbly batter.
Next, we spread the batter thinly on a hot pan until it turns golden.
Finally, we serve it with coconut chutney for a perfect, crunchy bite.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Diversity
narration: Every state has a unique dish that tells a story about its people.
Sharing a meal with friends and family makes every bite taste even better.
Think about it: What is your favorite dish that your family cooks at home?

scenes.title: Life Before Modern Houses
narration: Have you ever wondered how people lived before houses and grocery stores existed?
Thousands of years ago, early humans lived in caves or simple huts.
They did not have schools, so they learned by watching their families.

scenes.title: Finding Food Long Ago
narration: Early humans were hunters and gatherers who moved around to find food.
They collected wild fruits, nuts, and roots from the forest.
They also hunted animals to have enough food for the whole group.
They moved from place to place when the food in one area ran out.

scenes.title: Tools and Fire
narration: They made sharp tools from stones to help them cut and dig.
One big discovery was fire, which kept them warm and safe.
They cooked their food over the fire to make it taste better.
Fire also helped them see in the dark inside their caves.

scenes.title: Remembering the Past
narration: Early humans were very clever to survive without any modern technology.
They used nature for everything, from tools to their warm shelters.
Think about it: What is one thing you use today that they did not have?

scenes.title: A World of Colors
narration: Have you noticed how people in India wear different styles of clothes in different states?
Why do people wear such different things in Kashmir compared to Kerala?
Let us discover how weather and tradition shape what we wear today.

scenes.title: Weather and Fabric
narration: In cold places like Himachal Pradesh, people wear thick wool to stay warm.
In hot and humid states like Tamil Nadu, light cotton keeps the body cool.
Fabrics are chosen based on the sun and the season of the land.
We use local materials like silk from Mysore or jute from Bengal.

scenes.title: Celebrating with Style
narration: Rohan wears a crisp white dhoti for the festival of Pongal.
Priya wears a bright colorful lehenga-choli for the dance of Garba.
These special outfits show our family history and our festive spirit.

scenes.title: Our Beautiful Diversity
narration: India has many styles, like the saree, sherwani, or the simple kurta.
Every piece of clothing tells a story about the home it comes from.
Think about it: If you traveled to a new state, what would you wear?

scenes.title: The First Homes
narration: Have you ever wondered where people lived before there were big cities?
Long ago, families did not have supermarkets or easy water taps.
They looked for places that had everything they needed to survive.

scenes.title: The Power of Rivers
narration: People realized that living near a river was the best choice.
The river gave them fresh water to drink every single day.
It also helped them grow healthy crops like wheat and barley.
Rivers were like giant highways for trading goods with others.

scenes.title: Life in Ancient India
narration: Long ago, people settled near the mighty Indus River in India.
They built strong houses using baked mud bricks.
Farmers used the river water to grow food for their families.
They also made beautiful clay pots to store their grains.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Early people settled near rivers for water, farming, and travel.
These settlements grew into the first big civilizations in history.
Think about it: Why do you think most cities today are still near water?

Natural Resources: Water.title: Where Does Our Water Come From?

scenes.title: The Everyday Water Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in your tap comes from?
It starts high up in the mountains when it rains or snows.
This water travels down long paths to fill our rivers.

scenes.title: Nature’s Water Journey
narration: Water from rivers and lakes is our most important natural resource.
Sunlight warms the water, turning it into invisible mist.
This mist forms clouds that travel across the sky.
Finally, the clouds get heavy and drop rain back down.

scenes.title: Water in Our Lives
narration: In India, farmers use river water to grow tasty wheat and rice.
We also store rainwater in big tanks to use later.
Clean water is essential for drinking and keeping healthy.

scenes.title: Protecting Our Water
narration: Remember, water is a gift from nature that we must share.
Always turn off the tap to save every precious drop.
Think about it: What is one way you can save water at home today?

scenes.title: The Soil in Your Garden
narration: Have you ever dug into the ground in your garden or a park?
Do you wonder what that brown, crumbly stuff really is?
It is not just dirt, it is a home for plants and tiny creatures!

scenes.title: What Makes Soil?
narration: Soil is made of tiny bits of broken rocks.
It also has dead leaves and twigs that rot away.
These mix with water and air to help things grow.

scenes.title: Growing Mangoes in India
narration: Think of a juicy mango tree growing in a farm in Ratnagiri.
The roots pull water and minerals from the rich soil.
Without good soil, the tree would not have any fruit.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Soil is made of rocks, leaves, water, and air.
It is super important for every plant in India.
Think about it: what would happen to our food if all the soil disappeared?

scenes.title: The Forest Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered where the paper in your notebook comes from?
It all starts in the tall, beautiful forests of India.
Let us explore why these green spaces are so important for us.

scenes.title: Understanding Natural Resources
narration: A natural resource is something useful that comes from nature.
Forests are special because they give us wood, fruit, and medicine.
They also act like a giant green blanket that cleans our air.

scenes.title: Forests In Our Life
narration: Imagine a tiger roaming in the Sundarbans forest in West Bengal.
The trees provide a safe home for birds, monkeys, and insects.
Without forests, these animals would have nowhere to sleep or eat.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Forests give us air, food, and homes for many animals.
We must protect these treasures so they stay healthy forever.
Think about it: what is one way you can save paper today?

scenes.title: A Mystery in the Mud
narration: Have you ever found a shiny old coin or a broken piece of clay pot in your garden?
Anu found an old seal near the Indus River while playing in the dirt.
How did people live thousands of years ago before big cities were built?

scenes.title: The First Great Cities
narration: Long ago, people settled near rivers because they needed fresh water for their farms.
They built strong brick houses and planned straight streets for their neighborhoods.
This group of organized people living together is called a civilization.

scenes.title: Life by the Indus
narration: In the Indus Valley, farmers grew wheat and barley to feed their families.
They traded colorful beads and clay pots with other villages using river boats.
They even invented a special way of writing, though we still cannot read it today!

scenes.title: Why History Matters
narration: Civilizations teach us how to build cities, share tools, and live together peacefully.
Everything we do today started with the smart ideas of these ancient people.
If you could design your own city, what is the first thing you would build?

scenes.title: Where do things come from?
narration: Look at your shiny steel lunchbox, what is it made of?
Deep inside the Earth, there are special rocks called minerals.
Have you ever wondered how we get those treasures out?

scenes.title: What are minerals?
narration: Minerals are natural building blocks found in the ground.
We use them to make everything from coins to cars.
Some are soft like talc, and some are hard like diamonds.
India has lots of iron and coal buried deep down.

scenes.title: Getting the minerals out
narration: People dig deep holes called mines to find them.
Machines help us bring the heavy rocks to the surface.
Then, we clean them to get the pure metal out.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: Minerals come from the Earth and help us build our world.
We must use them carefully because they do not grow back.
Can you find three things in your house made from minerals?
